source_pdf: 312 Affidavits by Indians who accepted land patents under protest 1928 [2 of 3].pdf

extraction.Name: Thomas Tibbits
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not wish his patent to his 160 acre allotment at the time it was issued him; but that the Indian Agency told him that the land would be assessed for taxes, and finally sold for them, if he did not take the patent, so he accepted it
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: mortgaged the place to Henry Lang, of Rapid City, South Dakota, for $800.00; that, in 1923, being unable to make payment on the mortgage, Lang foreclosed
extraction.Buyer: Henry Lang, of Rapid City, South Dakota, for $800.00; foreclosed in 1923
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: kept the taxes paid up on his allotment as long as he could; and, in 1922, being behind on the taxes, he mortgaged the place; being unable to make payment on the mortgage, Lang foreclosed; he considers he got a poor price for his land, in fact, it actually all went for taxes
extraction.Occupation/Income: works for ranchers for his living, which constitutes his only income
extraction.NOTES: mentally competent, has pretty fair health; has a wife and five children to support, all of whom have good health; has never received any aid from the County, State nor the United States Government; allotment was 160 acres; mortgage taken out in 1922; document subscribed and sworn before notary December 14, 1928
